London, 12<sup>th</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**_Forecast 2009_** , the LBMA’s annual survey of opinions from precious metal participants on the direction of prices for the coming year, has been released.   For platinum, GFMS’ Executive Chairman Philip Klapwijk forecast for platinum a high of $1,440/oz and a low of $ 850/oz (average $1,090/oz) in 2009.  The average prices given by 25 contributors see a high of $1,263.25/oz and a low of $776.5/oz (average $995.6).  For palladium, Philip Klapwijk forecasts a high of $290/oz and a low of $175/oz (average $228/ oz); LBMA contributors see a high of $291.2/oz and a low of $161.15 (average $217.89). 

## _Source:  LBMA_ 

**China vehicles sales** may rise about 5 % this year, the slowest pace since 1998, as a slowing economy and rising job insecurity damps demand, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers said.  Sales of cars, trucks and busses rose 6.7 % last year to 9.38 million, the group said in a statement today. A year earlier, sales jumped 22%. Cars sales in Asia’s biggest auto market have fallen in four of the past five months, causing the government to consider tax cuts and other measures to revive demand. The slowdown is hurting domestic carmakers as well as overseas automakers such as GM and VW, which are counting on emerging markets to offset slumping U.S. and European demand. 

“The biggest factor affecting China’s auto market in 2009 is consumer confidence,” Dong Yang, the auto group’s secretary general, said in Beijing today. “The key is what kinds of measures the government will take and when.”  The country’s passenger-car sales fell 8 % in December to 584,600 cars, capping the slowest annual increase in at least nine years. For the full year, sales rose 7.3 % to 6.76 million.  Overall vehicle sales tumbled 12 % in December to 741,600. Car sales in India also dropped 7 % last month, as the global recession spreads into Asia. “Even with falling growth, China is still the market with biggest potential this year,” said Yu Bing, a Pingan Securities Co. analyst. “Foreign automakers may allocate more resources to China to tap that growth.” 

## _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Eskom’s Medupi** power station construction site in Limpopo province has been reopened on Monday, following a cholera scare last week.  Eskom spokesman Fani Zulu said that it seemed as if the majority of workers were back on site, but a roll call was still being taken to ensure that everyone was back at work. Zulu noted that Eskom still could not confirm whether there had been a cholera outbreak, but said that the utility had, nevertheless, taken preventative measures to ensure that no further outbreaks could occur.  The Medupi power station, which is expected to be completed in 2015, is South Africa’s first new coal power station in more than two decades.
